SECTION 307-01: Automatic Transmission/Transaxle

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY OF SUBASSEMBLIES

Null

A new torque converter must be installed if one or more of the following statements are true:

A torque converter malfunction has been detected based on completed diagnostic procedures.

Converter stud(s), impeller hub or bushing is damaged. (NOTE: Stud threads may be repaired using a "thread chaser").

If there is a discoloration of the torque converter (due to overheating).

The torque converter is found to be out of specification, when performing the following checks:

Torque converter insert check

Torque converter end play check

Torque converter turbine torque check

Torque converter leakage check

If there is evidence of transmission assembly damage or fluid contamination due to the following transmission or converter failure modes:

Major metallic failure

Multiple clutches or clutch plate failures

Sufficient component wear which results in metallic contamination

 Assembly 

Prepare the transaxle for assembly by proceeding with the following steps:

Clean all parts (except the friction plates, seals, and intermediate/overdrive band) in solvent.

Dry all parts with moisture-free regulated compressed air (do not use shop towels).

Lubricate all internal parts (including friction plates) with MERCON ® Multi-purpose automatic transmission fluid.

Order the required repair parts.

Make sure the complete assortment of selective thickness parts are on hand for adjustments during assembly:

Drive sprocket thrust washers

Driven sprocket thrust bearing shims

Differential case thrust bearing shims

Low/reverse clutch pressure plates

During assembly, use petroleum jelly to hold the parts in place (do not use grease).

When tightening fasteners, use an accurate torque wrench.

Lightly coat bolt and nut threads with automatic transmission fluid for correct installation torque specifications.

Install the intermediate and overdrive band assembly into the transaxle case.

General instructions:

The following instructions apply to the CD4E automatic transaxle with 2.5L engine.

 NOTE: The torque converter hub must fully engage with the transaxle pump drive gear.
Check the installation depth of the torque converter.

[FIGURE: E0005951.gif]

 CAUTION: The torque converter is heavy. Install the special tool before raising the transaxle.

SECTION 307-05: Automatic Transmission/Transaxle External Controls

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

External Controls

 Shift Cable 

The shift cable is a unit and is installed new as such during repair.

 Selector Lever 

 Selector Lever Positions

P

Park

For securing the vehicle. The engine can be startet. Caution: Engage only when the vehicle is stationary (the automatic transaxle will be locked; should be engaged when working on a vehicle when the engine is running).

The selector lever can only be moved out of position ”P" if the ignition lock is at position ”II" and the foot brake is depressed.

In an emergency (battery discharged) it can also be unlocked manually - see selector lever lock.

R

Reverse

Only engage when the vehicle is stationary and the engine is idling.

N

Neutral

The engine can be started - no power transfer to the driving wheels.

D

Gears 1 to 4 (with overdrive)

Position for normal driving. All four gears are shifted electronically. When the engine is stopped this mode of operation is automatically enabled. For driving with and without overdrive - see overdrive spring loaded button.

D

Gears 1 to 3 (without overdrive)

Position for normal driving, but without fourth gear. For driving with and without overdrive - see overdrive spring loaded button.

2

2nd gear

The automatic transaxle stays in second gear.

1

1st gear

The automatic transaxle stays in first gear.

 Selector Lever Lock 

[FIGURE: V1701050.gif]

The selector lever lock can be moved mechanically out of position ”P" when for example the battery is disconnected or completely discharged.

Using a ball point pen or similar item as an unlocking lever, push forwards and hold in position.

Move the selector lever out of position "P".

 NOTE: If the selector lever is moved back to ”P" it is re-locked.

 Overdrive Spring Loaded Button 

[FIGURE: V1701113.gif]

The overdrive function (preventing the transaxle from shifting into fourth gear) can be switched off using the spring loaded button on the selector lever knob. The corresponding indicator lamp in the instrument panel lights up showing that the overdrive function is switched off.

To activate overdrive funktion, press the button again and the lamp will go out.

 Selector Lever Spring Loaded Button 

[FIGURE: V1701114.gif]

To move the lever from park position and to engage ”R", ”2", or ”P", the ignition lock must be set to ”II", the foot brake must be depressed and the spring loaded side button pressed in.

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

External Controls

Because fault diagnosis starts as soon as the vehicle is taken in for repair we recommend the following procedure:

Check that the customer concern is clearly understood. As necessary reproduce the concern on the vehicle.

If the concern is not clearly understood carry out a road test and perform visual checks using the following table.

 WARNING: Danger of accident. Apply the parking brake. Shift the transaxle to ”P". Failure to follow these instructions can result in personal injury. 

 Visual Inspection Chart

Mechanical

Electrical

Visibly damaged or worn parts.

Loose or missing nuts or bolts.

Fuse.

Check all electrical connectors are firmly together and check them for corrosion.

If a concern can be identified with certainty by a visual check, correct it and test that the system operates normally.

If the concern cannot be identified with certainty, then use the following symptom chart to identify it.

 Symptom Chart 

 Symptom Chart 

Condition

Possible Sources

Action

The Shift Interlock System Does Not Release/Lock Properly

Circuitry open/shorted.

Damaged brake pedal position (BPP) switch.

Damaged gearshift lever.

Instrument interface module.

 Go To Pinpoint Test A .

The Shift Control is Out of Proper Gear Relationship

Shift linkage out of adjustment.

 Go To Pinpoint Test B .

The Control Linkage is Binding

Damaged/Loose ignition/shifter interlock cable.

 Go To Pinpoint Test C .

The Transaxle Control Switch is Not Operating Properly

Damaged gearshift lever.

Circuitry.

Damaged powertrain control module.

 Go To Pinpoint Test D .

The Indicator Lamp is Not Operating Properly

Circuitry.

Damaged instrument interface module.

Damaged powertrain control module.

 Go To Pinpoint Test E .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Manual Transaxle and Clutch

Manual Transaxle and Clutch - General Information

This section covers general procedures for diagnosis and testing the clutch system. For additional information, refer to Section 308-01 . For specified clutch system service procedures. For additional information, refer to Section 308-02 . For a complete description of the manual transaxle. For additional information, refer to Section 308-03 .

The clutch system includes:

Flywheel.

Clutch disc.

Clutch pressure plate.

Clutch master cylinder.

Clutch slave cylinder.

Clutch release fork.

Clutch release hub and bearing.

The clutch master cylinder transmits fluid pressure to the slave cylinder, which in turn moves the clutch release fork and the clutch release hub and bearing.

The clutch master cylinder uses brake fluid and shares a common reservoir with the brake master cylinder

The clutch is a single plate, dry-friction disc with a diaphragm-style spring clutch pressure plate. The clutch disc has a hub which is splined to the input shaft. The clutch disc has friction material where it contacts the flywheel and the clutch pressure plate. Torsion springs on the clutch disc help absorb the engine torque pulses. The clutch pressure plate applies pressure to the clutch disc, holding it tightly against the surface of the flywheel.

In the engaged position, the diaphragm spring holds the clutch pressure plate against the clutch disc, so that engine torque is transmitted to the input shaft. When the clutch pedal is depressed, the clutch release hub and bearing pushes the diaphragm spring center toward the flywheel. The diaphragm spring pivots at the fulcrum, relieving the load on the clutch pressure plate. Steel spring straps riveted to the clutch pressure plate cover pull the clutch pressure plate from the clutch disc, disengaging the engine torque from the transaxle and enabling the gears to be changed.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Manual Transaxle and Clutch

 Special Tool(s) 

[FIGURE: ST1993A.gif]

12 Volt UV Spot Lamp or equivalent

164-R0751

 Inspection and Verification - Clutch 

As fault diagnosis starts when repairs are taken on, the following procedure is recommended:

Check that the customer concern is clear. If necessary, reconstruct the concern on the vehicle.

If the concern cannot be reconstructed, perform a test drive and/or carry out a visual check with the aid of the following table:

 Visual Inspection Chart

Mechanical

Oil leaks - transaxle.

Visibly damaged or worn parts.

Loose or missing screws or nuts.

If the concern can be clearly identified by the visual check, the concern should be repaired and the system tested to see that it functions perfectly.

If the concern cannot be clearly identified, the following Symptom Chart should be used to identify it exactly.

 Inspection and Verification - MTX-75 

The following checks should be carried out before repairing or replacing the transaxle:

 Poor gear shifting 

Check the operation of the clutch: Lay a block of wood approx. 25 mm thick under the clutch pedal and depress the clutch pedal as far as the stop. If 1st or 2nd gear can be selected with no problem with the engine running and the parking brake applied, the clutch is OK. If the gear cannot be selected, repair the clutch.

Check the selector mechanism:

The free play in the gearshift lever must be no more than 15 mm.

If the gearshift lever free play is too great, check the gearshift cables and replace them if necessary.

If the gearshift lever free play is OK, adjust the gearshift linkage. For additional information, refer to Section 308-06 .

Check the transaxle fluid level and top up with Automatic Transmission Fluid ESD-M2C186-A if necessary.

 Transaxle noise 

If transaxle noises are reported, first check the transaxle fluid level. If damage has occurred due to a lack of fluid, replace the transaxle.

 Oil leakage 

Check that the leaking fluid is actually transaxle fluid and not hydraulic fluid (from the hydraulically operated clutch) or engine oil.

Check the transaxle fluid level and, if necessary, drain off any excess fluid.

Locate the oil leak with the aid of a fluorescent test fluid and a UV inspection lamp.

Clean the transaxle and the adjacent areas carefully before the road test.

 Symptom Chart 

Condition

Possible Sources

Action

Significant effort required when downshifting or synchronizer crashing

Gear synchronization is inadequate.

Install a complete set (synchronizer hub with synchronizer rings) and INSTALL two new gear wheels belonging to the synchronizer unit.

Because of various changes and the difficulty in estimating the level of wear, complete new installation (as described above) is recommended.

Gear jumps out of engagement while driving.

Manufacturing error (INCORRECT gear wheel toothing or synchronizer ring).

Selector fork.

Gearshift problems in different gears (stiff or partially seized).

 Check 

 WARNING: Brakes and clutch discs contain asbestos fibers. Avoid breathing dust. Breathing asbestos dust may cause asbestosis and cancer. 

 WARNING: Breathing asbestos dust is hazardous to your health. 

 WARNING: Dust and dirt present on wheel brake and clutch assemblies may contain asbestos fibers that are hazardous to health when made airborne by cleaning with compressed air or by dry brushing. 

 WARNING: Wheel brake assemblies and clutch facings should be cleaned using a vacuum cleaner recommended for use with asbestos fibers such as brake/clutch/service vacuum. Dust and dirt from vacuum should be disposed of in a manner that prevents dust exposure such as sealed bags. The bag must be labeled as per OSHA instructions and the trash hauler notified as to the bag's contents. 

 WARNING: If a vacuum suitable for asbestos is not available, cleaning should be done wet. If dust generation is still possible, technicians should wear government-approved toxic dust purifying respirators. 

 WARNING: Grinding or sanding on brake linings, pads, rotors, drums or clutch facings should be done only while using properly exhaust - ventilated equipment. 

 WARNING: OSHA requires areas where asbestos dust generation is possible to be isolated and posted with warning signs. Only technicians concerned with performing brake or clutch service should be present in the area.

The clutch transfers the engine torque to the transaxle.

The clutch consists of a clutch disc and a clutch pressure plate with a diaphragm spring, bolted to the flywheel.

When the clutch pedal is depressed, the torque from the engine to the transaxle is interrupted. When the clutch pedal is not depressed, the clutch is engaged. It is disengaged when the pedal is depressed.

Clutch Controls

[FIGURE: M1601026.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

-

Brake master cylinder reservoir

2

-

Clutch master cylinder

3

-

Clutch slave cylinder with integrated release bearing

A hydraulic clutch operating system is used on the Contour/Mystique. The brake master cylinder reservoir has a separate chamber and is used to supply the hydraulic clutch system.

When the clutch pedal is depressed, pressure builds up in the clutch master cylinder and the release bearing is actuated.

The hydraulic clutch system has the following advantages:

Automatic adjustment.

Low operating effort.

Minimal wear.

SECTION 308-03: Manual Transmission/Transaxle

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Manual Transaxle

Cut away View

[FIGURE: V1601160.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

-

Transaxle housing - clutch side

2

-

Input shaft

3

-

Differential

4

-

Output shaft

5

-

Reverse gear idler

6

-

Transaxle housing

7

-

Selector mechanism

The MTX - 75 manual transaxle is a ” 2-shaft transaxle".

MTX-75 means:

M: Manual.

T: Transaxle

X TransaXle (front wheel drive).

75 Distance between input and output shaft in mm.

The aluminum transaxle housing consists of two closed sections. The reinforcing ribs on the transaxle housing have been revised to reduce noise and vibration. As a result, the preload on the shafts and differential bearings has also increased.

To improve the lubrication of the third gear wheel, an additional drip plate has been fitted to the selector fork, allowing more transaxle fluid to drip onto the third gear synchronizer rings.

With the ” 2-shaft transaxle", all the gears are in permanent mesh. In each gear the required transaxle ratio is achieved by means of a pair of gears.

When the reverse gear is selected, the direction of the output shaft is changed by an idler gear.

The input and output shafts turn on taper roller bearings.

To further improve stability and gearshifting, the selector mechanism has been revised to incorporate a maintenance - free cable operating mechanism.

All the gears, including reverse, are bevel - cut, synchronized and turn on needle roller bearings.

First, second, and third gears have double synchronization. The advantages of this are that the transaxle operates quietly, gearshifts are smooth, and the assembly is compact and light weight.

 Input and Output Shaft 

Input and Output Shaft

Reverse gear wheel

In neutral, none of the gears are connected to the input or output shaft via the relevant synchronizer unit. No torque is transmitted to the differential.

The input and output shafts are each seated in one taper roller bearing in the transaxle housing section on the clutch side and one taper roller bearing in the transaxle housing section on the transaxle side.

The output shaft drive pinion is in constant engagement with the differential drive annulus.

The third and fourth gears and the third/fourth gear synchronizer are located on the input shaft. The teeth for first and second and reverse gear are an integral part of the input shaft.

The first, second, fifth and reverse gears and the first/second gear synchronizer and fifth/reverse gear synchronizer are located on the output shaft. The teeth for third and forth gear are an integral part of the output shaft.

Differential

The main components of the differential are:

Output gear wheel

Spur gear

Four pinions at right angles to one another

Differential housing with two taper roller bearings

The transaxle and differential are installed in a two - part aluminum housing which is flange - mounted to the engine.

The driveshafts have serrated teeth and are secured with a snap - ring.

The torque is transmitted from the spur gear to the driveshafts via two differential pinions mounted on the differential pinion shaft and the driveshaft pinions.

When cornering, the drive gears need to turn at different speeds as the road wheels travel different distances. This is achieved by means of the differential pinions which turn on their own shaft and mesh with the driveshaft pinions turning at different rates.

The reverse gear idler is driven by the input shaft. Its function is to reverse the direction of rotation of the output shaft in reverse gear.

The reverse gear idler is seated in a needle roller bearing on the idler shaft and also in a mounting.

Selector interlock mechanism

[FIGURE: V1601163.gif]

Item

The selector interlock mechanism and the selector finger are mounted on a sleeve in the selector mechanism housing and keep the selected gear engaged with the aid of a spring - loaded ball until another gear is selected.

The selector interlock mechanism has three positions.

The reversing lamp switch is mounted on the side of the selector mechanism housing.

Gearshift lever on the transmission

Cable guide

The MTX-75 manual transmission is equipped with a cable gearshift mechanism on the Contour/Mystique.

The shift cable is white and the selector cable is black.

In order to disconnect the cables from their brackets on the transmission and at the gear lever, twist the two halves of each bracket counterclockwise against each other.

Because they are jointly connected to the floor assembly, the selector and shift cables may only be installed newly as a pair.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

External Controls

To accurately diagnose problems, the following procedure is recommended:

Check that the customer concern is clear. As necessary, reproduce the concern on the vehicle.

If the concern cannot be reproduced, carry out a test drive and/or visual check with the aid of the following table:

 Visual Inspection Chart

Mechanical

Visibly damaged or worn parts.

Loose or missing bolts or nuts.

If the concern can be clearly identified by the visual check, it should be corrected and the system tested to see that it functions perfectly.

If the concern cannot be clearly identified, the following Symptom Chart should be used to identify it exactly.

 Symptom Chart 

 Symptom Chart 

Condition

Possible Sources

 Catalytic Converters 

The catalytic converter resembles a small muffler. Owing to the high temperatures at which the catalytic converter operates, the vehicle body areas around the catalytic converters are protected by heatshields. The catalytic converter controls three emissions; hydrocarbons (HC), carbon monoxide (CO) and oxides of nitrogen (NOx).

Fuel System

The Fuel System Components

[FIGURE: GV0905A.gif]

Item

Inertia fuel shutoff switch

Fuel is supplied at high pressure to the fuel injectors through a fuel injection supply manifold. For vehicles without a returnless fuel system, the fuel injection supply manifold is equipped with a fuel pressure regulator. For vehicles with a returnless fuel system, the fuel pressure regulator is integral to the fuel pump module. An inertia type fuel shutoff switch will cut power to the fuel pump in the event of an accident. The fuel lines are metal with flexible connections.

SECTION 310-00B: Fuel System - General Information

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel System

Component Locations

[FIGURE: A0006784.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

-

CNG tank

2

-

CNG tank filler valve

3

-

Solenoid valve

4

-

CNG tank filler pipe one-way valve

5

-

Fuel pressure regulator

6

-

Coalescer/filter

7

-

Quarter turn valve

 WARNING: Do not modify the system configuration or components, or replace components with parts not specially designed for use with natural gas. Ford Motor Company Ltd has specially designed the materials, components and system configuration for the 2.0L Contour compressed natural gas vehicles, and each particular system is precisely calibrated for efficient operation. The use of different parts or materials can produce an untested configuration that could result in fire, or cause engine damage. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel supply lines will remain pressurized after shutdown. When servicing fuel related components, do not smoke or carry lighted tobacco or any open flame of any type. Flammable gases may be present and ignite. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel system pressure release is required prior to fuel system component service. The fuel tank must be evacuated prior to tank removal. Removal of components without pressure release or tank evacuation can cause natural gas to escape into the air. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Eye and ear protection are required to be worn during venting or removal and installation of fuel system components. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Do not evacuate any fuel tank unless the fuel tank or fuel tank solenoid valve is damaged or inoperative and a new fuel tank solenoid valve or fuel tank must be installed. Unnecessary evacuating of good tanks can cause damage to the fuel tank solenoid valve. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Always ground the vehicle and natural gas system. High pressure gas escaping can cause static electricity buildup and subsequent sparking. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Never attempt to tighten or adjust fittings while system is under pressure. Close solenoid valve manual shutoff and release system pressure. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: All compressed natural gas lines must be installed prior to returning the manual shutoff valve to normal operation. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: The fuel system is always pressurized to 689 kpa (100 psi) from the fuel pressure regulator to the compuvalve and up to 20700 kpa (3000 psi) upstream of the fuel pressure regulator. Use care when servicing the fuel system. Fuel pressure must be released prior to any fuel system service. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 CAUTION: If the CNG system is being disconnected for an extended length of time, cover all open hose fittings and electrical connections to avoid contamination. 

The compressed natural gas system consists of, a gas regulator, a combined metering valve and computer (compuvalve), a gas supply manifold, a selector switch to facilitate communication, and an alternative fuels control module (AFCM) to exchange data with the powertrain control module (PCM). Incorporated into the compuvalve are absolute pressure sensors (fuel and intake manifold) and a fuel temperature sensor. The system operation may be summarized as follows:

Fuel from the natural gas fuel tank flows through a coalescer filter to the high-pressure regulator.

The regulator provides a consistent operating fuel pressure 690 kpa (100 psi) for the system.

The fuel is passed to the compuvalve, which electronically meters fuel according to demand, and controls spark advance for optimum power. The inputs from the PCM are used to dynamically monitor the engine and environment to provide closed loop control of fueling.

The fuel is then introduced into the air intake manifold through the fuel supply lines.

Fuel Pressure Regulator

High pressure compressed natural gas (CNG) enters the single stage regulator and is delivered to the compuvalve at a consistent pressure of 690 kpa (100 psi).

Coalescer/Filter

CNG vehicles are equipped with a coalescer/filter assembly which separates, filters, and stores any contamination and moisture found in the fuel system, preventing moisture from entering the engine.

Quarter Turn Valve

The quarter turn valve is a manual valve used to isolate the CNG control system from the tank assembly. The valve is open while the handle is parallel to the underbody and closed while perpendicular to the underbody.

Fuel Tank Filler Pipe One-Way Valve

This valve is located on the intake port leading to the solenoid valve.

Fuel Tank Filler Valve

The fuel tank filler valve is located in the fuel filler housing located on the driver side rear quarter panel.

Compressed Natural Gas Tank

The tank used for compressed natural gas is designed and manufactured to meet requirements of NGV2 standards as adopted by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and the American Gas Association (AGA). The tank is graded as NGV-2 type and consists of a metal liner reinforced with resin impregnated continuous filament. The filament is "hoop wrapped" which means that the winding of filament is done in a substantially circular pattern around the cylindrical portion of the liner, and is rated for use at 20700 kpa (3000 psi). Tanks should never be overpressured.

Solenoid Valve

The integral venting tank valve is operated by an electrical solenoid. The solenoid is activated when switched battery voltage is applied and the valve is opened. For service a manual shutoff is built into the valve. For additional information, refer to procedure Fuel Tank Evacuation in this section.

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Fuel System Service Precautions

 WARNING: Do not modify the system configuration or components, or install components not specially designed for use with alternative fuels. Ford Motor Company Ltd has specially designed the materials, components and system configuration for alternative fuel vehicles, and each particular system is precisely calibrated for efficient operation. The use of incorrect parts or materials can produce an untested configuration that could result in fire, or cause engine damage. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel supply lines will remain pressurized after shutdown. When servicing fuel related components, do not smoke or carry lighted tobacco or any open flame of any type. Flammable gases may be present and ignite. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel system pressure release is required prior to fuel system component service. The fuel tank must be evacuated prior to tank removal. Removal of components without pressure release or tank evacuation can cause gas to escape into the air. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Eye, hand and ear protection are required to be worn during depressurizing or removal and installation of fuel system components. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Do not evacuate any fuel tank unless the fuel tank or fuel tank solenoid valve is damaged or inoperative and a new fuel tank solenoid valve or fuel tank must be installed. Unnecessary evacuating of good tanks can cause damage to the fuel tank solenoid valve. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Always ground the vehicle and alternative fuel system. High pressure gas escaping can cause static electricity buildup and subsequent sparking. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Never attempt to tighten or adjust fittings while system is pressurized. Close the solenoid valve manual shutoff and release system pressure. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: All gas lines must be installed prior to reconnecting the battery. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: (Contour CNG Only) The fuel system is always pressurized to 689 kpa (100 psi) from the fuel pressure regulator to the compuvalve and up to 20700 kpa (3000 psi) upstream of the fuel pressure regulator. Use care when servicing the fuel system. Fuel pressure must be released prior to any fuel system service. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 CAUTION: If the alternative fuel system is being disconnected for an extended length of time, cover all open hose fittings and electrical connections to avoid contamination.

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Fuel Tank Inspection

 WARNING: Do not modify the system configuration or components, or replace components with parts not specially designed for use with natural gas. Ford Motor Company Ltd has specially designed the materials, components and system configuration for the 2.0L Contour compressed natural gas vehicles, and each particular system is precisely calibrated for efficient operation. The use of different parts or materials can produce an untested configuration that could result in fire, or cause engine damage. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel supply lines will remain pressurized after shutdown. When servicing fuel related components, do not smoke or carry lighted tobacco or any open flame of any type. Flammable gases may be present and ignite. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel system pressure release is required prior to fuel system component service. The fuel tank must be evacuated prior to tank removal. Removal of components without pressure release or tank evacuation can cause natural gas to escape into the air. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Eye and ear protection are required to be worn during venting or removal and installation of fuel system components. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Do not evacuate any fuel tank unless the fuel tank or fuel tank solenoid valve is damaged or inoperative and a new fuel tank solenoid valve or fuel tank must be installed. Unnecessary evacuating of good tanks can cause damage to the fuel tank solenoid valve. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Always ground the vehicle and natural gas system. High pressure gas escaping can cause static electricity buildup and subsequent sparking. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Never attempt to tighten or adjust fittings while system is under pressure. Close solenoid valve manual shutoff and release system pressure. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: All compressed natural gas lines must be installed prior to returning the manual shutoff valve to normal operation. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: The fuel system is always pressurized to 689kpa (100 psi) from the fuel pressure regulator to the compuvalve and up to 20700 kpa (3000 psi) upstream of the fuel pressure regulator. Use care when servicing the fuel system. Fuel pressure must be released prior to any fuel system service. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Never discharge gas by just opening the tank valves. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: A new fuel tank must installed, if the original one does not pass the inspection criteria, before the vehicle is returned to service using compressed natural gas. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 NOTE: The following procedure is an in-vehicle, visual inspection for compressed natural gas fuel tanks. Fuel tanks must be visually inspected every 36 months or 58,000 km (36,000 miles) which ever occurs first in order to maintain compliance with NGV2 standards.

 NOTE: The external inspection is for external damage and deterioration and must be carried out by qualified personnel in accordance with the manufacturers established inspection criteria and the procedures outlined in pamphlet C-6.2 from the Compressed Gas Association (CGA).

 NOTE: The Compressed Natural Gas pamphlet C-6.2 can be obtained from the CGA at 1752 Jefferson Davis Highway, Arlington, VA 22202-4102. Phone: (703)412-0900 ext. 799 Fax: (703)412-0128

 NOTE: Tanks that have been subjected to the stress of vehicular accidents must be inspected and approved prior to being returned to service. Tanks that have been subject to fire must be condemned and removed from service.

Remove the tank shield from the luggage compartment.

[FIGURE: A0006794.gif]

Examine the vehicle body and chassis in the general area near the fuel tank for indication of collision damage, malfunction, or fire.

Examine the fuel labels for the tank expiration date. Use a light and mirror to access labels hidden from normal view. If the expiration date has been exceeded, condemn the tank, using the procedure

Inspect the tank sidewall and dome ends, following the general guidelines set forth in the CGA pamphlet C-6.2. Inspect the tank for the following:

abrasions

dents

cracking, blistering or peeling of clear coating

corrosion

cracks or gouges in the metal dome

cracks in the fiberglass overwrap

exposed fibers

delamination (separating) of the fiberglass overwrap

discoloration of the fiberglass overwrap

fire or heat damage, such as charring or discoloration

impact damage (cracking) in the fiberglass overwrap

cuts or gouges in the fiberglass overwrap

If any flaws are detected, measure the depth and length of the flaw in accordance with the CGA pamphlet C-6.2 guidelines. If any of the flaws cannot be completely measured in the vehicle, the tank must be removed from the vehicle for further inspection.

If the tank has been or is suspected of having been exposed to a corrosive chemical spill, the tank must be removed from the vehicle for further inspection of the complete composite surface, including the area under the tank straps. If there is any indication of chemical attack , such as blistering, cracking or delamination, the tank must be condemned and a new tank installed. The tank on the Contour equipped with CNG is of a NGV2-2 design and does not have to be hydrostatically tested during their service life.

Condemned tanks, whether due to damage or expiration, shall be removed from the vehicle and destroyed as follows:

Remove the fuel tank. For additional information, refer to Section 310-01A . For additional information, refer to Section 310-01B .

Purge the fuel tank with compressed air for 30 seconds.

Destroy the fuel tank by drilling a 12.7-mm (0.50-inch) diameter hole in the fuel tank sidewall.

Fuel tank straps: Examine the fuel tank straps for correct positioning of the rubber isolators. Replace the rubber isolators as necessary.

Inspection record: Record the date, vehicle mileage and the results of the fuel tank inspection.

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

SECTION 310-01A: Fuel Tank and Lines

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank and Lines

[FIGURE: V2304155.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

Fuel tank

2

Fuel filter

3

Fuel tank filler pipe

4

Fuel tank ventilation

5

Fuel tank roll-over valve

6

Fuel tank pressure sensor

7

Fuel pump

The fuel supply system consists of:

 Fuel Tank 

The fuel tank is of plastic construction and is retained to the vehicle by means of two steel support straps. The fuel tank support straps are hooked onto the underside of the vehicle chassis towards the rear of the fuel tank and bolt to the vehicle towards the front of the fuel tank. Fuel tank ventilation is achieved through a fuel tank roll-over valve into an evaporative emission canister which absorbs the fuel vapour. The fuel tank roll-over valve will prevent fuel loss from the fuel tank if the vehicle becomes inverted.

 Fuel Filter 

The fuel filter is of conventional construction being that of a paper element sealed within a steel canister. The fuel filter is located on the leading edge of the fuel tank.

 Fuel Tank Filler Pipe 

The fuel tank filler pipe is of steel construction and is retained to the vehicle by means of two lower retaining bolts and one upper retaining bolt. The fuel tank filler pipe is fitted with a twist-fit filler cap, which seals the system.

 Fuel Pump 

The fuel pump is an electric roller cell pump which is located inside the fuel tank. The fuel pump features an integral fuel tank sender unit and is fixed to the fuel tank by means of a locking ring.

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

SECTION 310-01B: Fuel Tank and Lines - Compressed Natural Gas

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank and Lines

Component Locations

[FIGURE: A0006783.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

Compressed natural gas (CNG) tank

2

Fuel tank filler valve

3

Solenoid valve

4

Fuel tank filler pipe one-way valve

5

Fuel pressure regulator

6

Fuel pressure regulator filter element

7

Fuel tank pressure (FTP) sensor

8

Quarter turn valve

9

Coalescer/filter

 WARNING: Do not modify the system configuration or components, or replace components with parts not specially designed for use with natural gas. Ford Motor Company Ltd has specially designed the materials, components and system configuration for the 2.0L Contour compressed natural gas vehicles, and each particular system is precisely calibrated for efficient operation. The use of different parts or materials can produce an untested configuration that could result in fire, or cause engine damage. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel supply lines will remain pressurized after shutdown. When servicing fuel related components, do not smoke or carry lighted tobacco or any open flame of any type. Flammable gases may be present and ignite. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Fuel system pressure release is required prior to fuel system component service. The fuel tank must be evacuated prior to tank removal. Removal of components without pressure release or tank evacuation can cause natural gas to escape into the air. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Eye and ear protection are required to be worn during venting or removal and installation of fuel system components. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Do not evacuate any fuel tank unless the fuel tank or fuel tank solenoid valve is damaged or inoperative and a new fuel tank solenoid valve or fuel tank must be installed. Unnecessary evacuating of good tanks can cause damage to the fuel tank solenoid valve. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Always ground the vehicle and natural gas system. High pressure gas escaping can cause static electricity buildup and subsequent sparking. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Never attempt to tighten or adjust fittings while system is under pressure. Close solenoid valve manual shutoff and release system pressure. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: All compressed natural gas lines must be installed prior to returning the manual shutoff valve to normal operation. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: The fuel system is always pressurized to 689 kpa (100 psi) from the fuel pressure regulator to the compuvalve and up to 20700 kpa (3000 psi) upstream of the fuel pressure regulator. Use care when servicing the fuel system. Fuel pressure must be released prior to any fuel system service. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 CAUTION: If the CNG system is being disconnected for an extended length of time, cover all open hose fittings and electrical connections to avoid contamination. 

CNG Tank

The tank used for compressed natural gas is designed and manufactured to meet requirements of NGV2 standards as adopted by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and the American Gas Association (AGA). The tank is graded as NGV-2 type and consists of a metal liner reinforced with resin impregnated continuous filament. The filament is "hoop wrapped" which means that the winding of filament is done in a substantially circular pattern around the cylindrical portion of the liner, and is rated for use at 20700 kpa (3000 psi). Tanks should never be overpressured.

Fuel Tank Filler Valve

The fuel tank filler valve is located behind the fuel filler door inside the fuel filler compartment and provides a receptacle for the fueling connection.

Fuel Tank Filler Pipe One-Way Valve

This valve is located on the intake port leading to the solenoid valve. The arrow on the valve should always point towards the solenoid valve.

Solenoid Valve

The integral venting tank valve is operated by an electrical solenoid. The solenoid is activated when switched battery voltage is applied and the valve is opened. For service, a manual shutoff is built into the valve.

Fuel Pressure Regulator

High-pressure compressed natural gas (CNG) enters the single stage regulator and is delivered to the compuvalve at a consistent pressure of 690 kpa (100 psi).

Fuel Pressure Regulator Filter Element

The fuel pressure regulator has a secondary filter element located where the high-pressure CNG line enters from the coalescer/filter assembly.

Fuel Tank Pressure (FTP) Sensor

The FTP sensor is located in the center of the pressure regulator and provides indication to the compuvalve that the tank has pressure 0 to 20700 kpa (0 to 3000 psi) in order to operate the fuel gauge.

Quarter Turn Valve

The quarter turn valve is a manual valve used to isolate the CNG control system from the tank assembly. The valve is open while the handle is parallel to the high pressure fuel lines and closed while perpendicular to the fuel lines.

Coalescer/Filter

CNG vehicles are equipped with a coalescer/filter assembly which separates, filters, and stores any contamination and moisture found in the fuel system, preventing moisture from entering the engine.

Removal of components without pressure release or tank evacuation can cause natural gas to escape into the air. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Eye and ear protection are required to be worn during venting or removal and installation of fuel system components. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Do not evacuate any fuel tank unless the fuel tank or fuel tank solenoid valve is damaged or inoperative and a new fuel tank solenoid valve or fuel tank must be installed. Unnecessary evacuating of good tanks can cause damage to the fuel tank solenoid valve. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Always ground the vehicle and natural gas system. High pressure gas escaping can cause static electricity buildup and subsequent sparking. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Never attempt to tighten or adjust fittings while system is under pressure. Close solenoid valve manual shutoff and release system pressure. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: All compressed natural gas lines must be installed prior to returning the manual shutoff valve to normal operation. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: The fuel system is always pressurized to 689 kpa (100 psi) from the fuel pressure regulator to the compuvalve and up to 20700 kpa (3000 psi) upstream of the fuel pressure regulator. Use care when servicing the fuel system. Fuel pressure must be released prior to any fuel system service. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 CAUTION: If the CNG system is being disconnected for an extended length of time, cover all open hose fittings and electrical connections to avoid contamination. 

 NOTE: Lightly coat all O-rings with Dow Corning 55 O-ring lubricant or equivalent.
Install a new medium-size O-ring.

[FIGURE: E0007892.gif]

Remove protective cap from the new assembly and position into core wrench.

 NOTE: If the spring is out of position, the assembly will not tighten fully into valve body.
Carefully hold the piston assembly and tool together and place into the valve body and hand tighten.

Tighten the piston assembly to 40 Nm (30 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A0006773.gif]

Install a new small O-ring over the shaft and a large O-ring into the ring.

[FIGURE: E0007893.gif]

Tighten the ring to 20 Nm (15 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A0006774.gif]

Tighten the solenoid coil and nut to 7 Nm (62 lb-in).

[FIGURE: A0006800.gif]

Tighten the gyrolok nut until snug then tighten an additional 1/2 turn.

Reconnect electrical connector J/P120.

Reset manual shutoff to normal operation.

 NOTE: When the battery is disconnected and reconnected, some abnormal drive symptoms may occur while the vehicle relearns its adaptive strategy. The vehicle may need to be driven to relearn the strategy.
Reconnect the battery ground cable.

Turn the ignition key ON, wait five seconds then turn the ignition key OFF.

Pressurize the CNG system and inspect fittings for leaks. For additional information, refer to Section 310-00A . For additional information, refer to Section 310-00B .

Install the ribbed hoses and clamps to the tank valve.

Install the tank cover.

Removal of components without pressure release or tank evacuation can cause natural gas to escape into the air. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Eye and ear protection are required to be worn during venting or removal and installation of fuel system components. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Do not evacuate any fuel tank unless the fuel tank or fuel tank solenoid valve is damaged or inoperative and a new fuel tank solenoid valve or fuel tank must be installed. Unnecessary evacuating of good tanks can cause damage to the fuel tank solenoid valve. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Always ground the vehicle and natural gas system. High pressure gas escaping can cause static electricity buildup and subsequent sparking. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: Never attempt to tighten or adjust fittings while system is under pressure. Close solenoid valve manual shutoff and release system pressure. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: All compressed natural gas lines must be installed prior to returning the manual shutoff valve to normal operation. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: The fuel system is always pressurized to 689 kpa (100 psi) from the fuel pressure regulator to the compuvalve and up to 20700 kpa (3000 psi) upstream of the fuel pressure regulator. Use care when servicing the fuel system. Fuel pressure must be released prior to any fuel system service. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 CAUTION: If the CNG system is being disconnected for an extended length of time, cover all open hose fittings and electrical connections to avoid contamination. 

 NOTE: When the battery is disconnected and reconnected, some abnormal drive symptoms may occur while the vehicle relearns its adaptive strategy. The vehicle may need to be driven 16 km (10 miles) or more to relearn the strategy.

 NOTE: Reassemble using the a new filter kit.

 NOTE: Tighten the gyrolok fitting until snug then tighten an additional 1/2 turn.
To install, reverse the removal procedure.

 WARNING: All compressed natural gas lines must be installed prior to returning the manual shutoff valve to normal operation. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury. 

 WARNING: The fuel system is always pressurized to 689 kpa (100 psi) from the fuel pressure regulator to the compuvalve and up to 20700 kpa (3000 psi) upstream of the fuel pressure regulator. Use care when servicing the fuel system. Fuel pressure must be released prior to any fuel system service. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury. 

 CAUTION: If the CNG system is being disconnected for an extended length of time, cover all open hose fittings and electrical connections to avoid contamination. 

 NOTE: When the battery is disconnected and reconnected, some abnormal drive symptoms may occur while the vehicle relearns its adaptive strategy. The vehicle may need to be driven to relearn the strategy.

 NOTE: O-rings should be coated lightly with an O-ring lubricant before installing, do not use a silicone based grease.

 NOTE: If adapter loosens when removing sensor, remove and replace the O-ring, then reinstall to torque specified.

To install, reverse the removal procedure.

[FIGURE: A0006812.gif]

[FIGURE: A0006810.gif]

Tighten the gyrolok fitting until snug and tighten an additional 1/2 turn.

Pressurize the CNG system and inspect fittings for leaks. For additional information, refer to Section 310-00A . For additional information, refer to Section 310-00B .

SECTION 310-02: Acceleration Control

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Acceleration Control

The acceleration control system consists of an accelerator pedal and an accelerator cable. The driver controls throttle demand by using the pedal mounted in the passenger compartment which is connected to the throttle body by the cable. Pedal return is achieved by the use of a throttle return spring.

SECTION 310-03: Speed Control

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Speed Control

Contour shown, Mystique similar

[FIGURE: V3305060.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

Speed control actuator cable

2

Speed control actuator switches

3

Speed control actuator

4

Clutch pedal position switch.

5

Vehicle speed sensor

6

Brake pedal switches

The speed control system is operated by means of five switches on the steering wheel. The functions are:

Switch

Function

ON

Activate system

OFF

De-activate system

SET/ACC

Accelerate and tap-up

COAST

Coast and tap down

RES

Resume

The control unit provides signals to the stepper motor housed in the actuator. The stepper motor moves the throttle body cam by means of an internal geartrain and a cable linkage. The vehicle speed sensor generates the reference signal that the control unit compares to the speed setting selected by the driver. If a discrepancy exists the stepper motor will adjust the throttle body cam setting, correcting the vehicle's speed.

Any of the switches operated by the brake or clutch pedal will interrupt the speed control operation by releasing the speed control actuator cable and returning the throttle body cam to idle.

 Speed Control Actuator 

[FIGURE: V3305001.gif]

The speed control actuator is mounted on the right-hand inner fender behind the suspension unit top mount. The speed control actuator incorporates the following components:

The electronic speed control unit

The stepper motor and geartrain, electromagnetic coupling and reduction gearing

 Speed Control Unit 

[FIGURE: V3305002.gif]

The speed control unit evaluates incoming signals from the system sensors and switches. It actuates a stepper motor and cable linkage to adjust the throttle body cam, maintaining a constant vehicle road speed.

If the vehicles brake or the clutch pedal are depressed, the speed control unit interrupts the speed control operation.

 Stepper Motor 

[FIGURE: V3305003.gif]

When the speed control system is activated, the windings in the stepper motor are energized by the speed control unit ensuring accurate positioning of the throttle body cam. The vehicle road speed then settles to the speed selected by the driver.

 Actuator Switches 

[FIGURE: V3305061.gif]

When the ON switch is pressed and the vehicle is travelling at a speed greater than 25 mph the speed control system will accept speed inputs.

[FIGURE: V3305062.gif]

Pressing the SET/ACC switch at any speed in excess of 25 mph causes the vehicle to accelerate or maintain the present speed. The switch can be used in two ways.

Press the SET/ACC switch and hold it down until the vehicle reaches the desired speed. When released, the speed is stored in the memory and used to maintain the vehicle speed.

Press the SET/ACC witch repeatedly in order to increase the road speed in steps of approximately1 mph.

[FIGURE: V3305063.gif]

The COAST switch is used to reduce the vehicle's road speed. The switch can be used in two ways:

Press and hold it down until the vehicle slows to the desired speed. When the switch is released, the speed is stored in the memory and used to maintain the vehicle speed.

Press repeatedly to reduce the vehicle road speed in steps of approximately 1 mph.

[FIGURE: V3305064.gif]

Pressing the RES switch automatically resumes control at the set speed.

[FIGURE: V3305065.gif]

Pressing the OFF switch deactivates the speed control system. The speed setting stored in the speed control unit memory will be erased.

 Stop Lamp Switch , Brake Pedal 

[FIGURE: V3305010.gif]

If the brakes are applied while the speed control system is active, the speed control unit receives a signal from the stop lamp switch. This causes the stepper motor to close the throttle body cam under stepper motor control.

 Deactivator Switch, Brake Pedal 

[FIGURE: V3305010.gif]

If the brakes are applied forcibly while the speed control system is active, the control unit receives a signal from the deactivator switch. This causes, the electromagnetic actuated coupling on the stepper motor to immediately disconnect the motor from the throttle body cam allowing, the cable and throttle body cam to close rapidly under throttle return spring control.

 Clutch Pedal Position Switch 

[FIGURE: V3305010.gif]

When the clutch pedal is depressed, the clutch pedal position switch causes the electromagnetic actuated coupling on the stepper motor to immediately disconnect the motor from the throttle body cam, allowing the cable and throttle body cam to close under throttle return spring control.

SECTION 211-00: Steering System - General Information

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering System

[FIGURE: M1301001.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

-

Steering wheel

2

-

Steering column

-

Flexible coupling

4

-

Tie - rod end

5

-

Tie - rod

6

-

Steering gear boot

7

-

Steering gear

 Steering Column 

The steering system consists of a steering wheel that encases the air bag module. The steering wheel is attached to the steering column assembly with a single retaining bolt. The steering gear pinion is connected to the steering column through a flexible coupling. The coupling is fixed to the pinion with a pinch bolt and to the column with a clamp plate and bolt.

 Steering Gear 

The power steering gear is of the conventional rack and pinion type. There are two steering gears used:

62.3 mm rack travel for SVT vehicles fitted with 205/55 R16 tires.

67.8 mm rack travel for all other tires with I4.

66.3 mm rack travel for V6 models.

SVT Only

The SVT steering gear has internal travel restrictors that allow the larger tires to be used without interference problems.

 Power Steering Pump 

Hydraulic fluid under pressure is supplied to the steering gear by a hydraulic pump. The pump has a remote reservoir which is attached to the strut tower at the upper right - hand corner of the engine compartment.

Incorrect tire size or different tire/tread type.

INSTALL new tires as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-04 .

Vehicle is unevenly or excessively loaded.

ADJUST load evenly.

Incorrect wheel alignment.

ADJUST the wheel alignment as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-00 .

Damaged front suspension components.

INSTALL new front suspension components as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-01 .

Damaged rear suspension components.

INSTALL new rear suspension components as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-02 .

Steering gear valve effort out of balance.

SHIFT transaxle into Neutral while driving at not more than 50 km/h (30 mph) and turn ignition to position I (ACC), (engine off - coasting). If vehicle does not pull with the engine off, INSTALL a new power steering gear. For additional information, refer to Section 211-02 .

If vehicle does drift with engine off, CROSS SWITCH front tire/wheel assemblies.

If vehicle pulls to opposite side, CRISS - CROSS tire/wheel assemblies that were on the rear to same side on the front.

If vehicle pull direction is not changed, CHECK front suspension components and wheel alignment. For additional information, refer to Section 204-01 .

Check front and rear brakes for correct operation.

INSTALL new brake components as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 206-00 .

Check for bent rear suspension components and for damaged or sagging coil springs in the front or the rear suspension.

INSTALL new front suspension components as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-01 .

INSTALL new rear suspension components as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-02 .

Check rear suspension for loose or worn suspension components or rear suspension retaining bolts.

INSTALL new rear suspension components as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-02 .

TIGHTEN all retaining bolts. For additional information, refer to Section 204-02 .

Feedback (whining or knocking noises in steering gear) – condition where roughness is felt in the steering wheel by the driver when the vehicle is driven over rough surfaces

Steering column shaft coupling joints.

INSTALL a new steering column as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 211-04 .

Loose/worn front wheel spindle, tie - rods or tie - rod ends.

INSTALL a new tie - rod or tie - rod end as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 211-03 .

Steering gear retaining bolts loose or damaged.

TIGHTEN/INSTALL new bolts as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 211-02 .

Steering column to flexible coupling bolt loose.

TIGHTEN bolt(s). For additional information, refer to Section 211-04 .

Loose suspension/bushing, retaining bolts or ball joints.

TIGHTEN/INSTALL new components as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-01 .

Steering column shaft worn.

INSTALL a new steering column. For additional information, refer to Section 211-04 .

Steering fails to return to center, following a turn, without manual effort from the driver. In addition, when the driver returns the steering wheel to center, it may have a sticky or catchy feel

Incorrect tire pressure.

ADJUST tire pressures as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-04 .

Incorrect tire size or incorrect type.

INSTALL new tires as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 204-04 .

Misaligned steering column tube or column shroud rubbing steering wheel.

ALIGN steering column tube. For additional information, refer to Section 211-04 .

Steering column shaft binding.

INSTALL a new steering column. For additional information, refer to Section 211-04 .

Steering column shaft floor seal torn.

INSTALL a new floor seal as necessary. For additional information, refer to Section 211-04 .

Binding or damage to tie - rods.

SECTION 211-00: Steering System - General Information

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Power Steering System Bleeding

 Special Tool(s) 

[FIGURE: ST1176A.gif]

Hand Vacuum Pump, or equivalent

416 - D002 (D95L - 7559 - A)

 Bleeding 

 NOTE: When filling or topping up the reservoir, make sure that the fluid is clean and not agitated prior to use. The fluid should be poured slowly into the reservoir to minimize the possibility of aeration.
Fill up the power steering reservoir to the MAX mark.

[FIGURE: M1301020.gif]

 NOTE: When bleeding the system make sure that the fluid in the reservoir does not fall below the MIN mark, as air may enter the system.
Start the engine and slowly turn the steering wheel from stop - to - stop.

Examine the hose connections, steering gear boots and valve body for external leaks.

Switch off the engine and check the fluid level. Fill up the power steering reservoir to the MAX mark as necessary.

Check the system for leaks.

Using the special tool, apply a vacuum of 51 kPa (15 in Hg) to the power steering reservoir.

[FIGURE: V1301155.gif]

 NOTE: When bleeding the system the vacuum will decrease, maintain a sufficient vacuum of 51 kPa (15 in Hg) using the vacuum pump. If the vacuum decreases by more than 7 kPa (2 in Hg) in five minutes the system should be checked for leaks.
Bleed the system.

Start the engine and slowly turn the steering wheel to the right, just off the stop.

Turn the engine off and apply a vacuum of 51 kPa (15 in Hg) using the vacuum pump, maintain the vacuum until the air is purged from the system (minimum of five minutes).

Release the vacuum at the vacuum pump.

Repeat the bleed procedure, turning the steering wheel to the left, just off the stop.

Remove the vacuum pump and stopper and fill the power steering reservoir as necessary.

Start the engine, turn the steering wheel from stop - to - stop. If excessive noise is apparent repeat the bleed procedure.

If the noise level is still unacceptable, leave the vehicle standing overnight then repeat the bleed procedure.

SECTION 211-02: Power Steering

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Steering

[FIGURE: M1301001.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

-

Steering wheel

2

-

Steering column

3

-

Flexible coupling

4

-

Tie - rod end

5

-

Tie - rod

6

-

Steering gear boot

7

-

Steering gear

The power steering gear is a conventional rack and pinion type. There are two steering gears used:

62.3 mm rack travel for SVT vehicles fitted with 205/55 R16 tires.

67.8 mm rack travel for all other tires with I4.

66.3 mm rack travel for V - 6 vehicles.

The steering gear is mounted on the front subframe assembly.

Hydraulic fluid under pressure is supplied to the steering gear by a hydraulic pump. The pump has a remote reservoir which is attached to the strut tower at the upper right - hand corner of the engine compartment.

Tie - rod

SECTION 211-04: Steering Column

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Column

[FIGURE: GG1108A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Steering column

Flexible coupling

The steering column is attached, at the lower end, to a flexible coupling by means of a clamp plate and bolt. The flexible coupling is attached to the steering gear pinion shaft with a pinch bolt. The flexible coupling entry into the engine compartment through the bulkhead is protected by a floor seal.

The steering column incorporates a multi - position steering lock with a high security lock barrel. The steering column assembly is fitted to the in - vehicle cross beam with four bolts.

All vehicles have an adjustable tilt steering column which is operated by a lever on the left - hand side of the column.

A worn or damaged steering column cannot be repaired, install a new steering column.

SECTION 211-05: Steering Column Switches

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Column Switches

[FIGURE: V1301508.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

-

Multifunction switch

2

-

Hazard/flasher switch

3

-

Wiper/washer switch

4

-

Ignition switch

5

-

Ignition switch lock cylinder

 Multifunction Switch 

The multifunction switch, located on the left - hand side of the steering column, controls the following:

hazard/flasher lamps

turn signal lamps

headlamp high beam

headlamp flash feature

To activate high beam, move the lever away from the steering wheel to the stop position. To activate the headlamp flash feature move the lever towards the steering wheel.

The hazard flasher system is an integral part of the multifunction switch. The system operates independently from the ignition switch. The flasher indicator system is deactivated when the hazard flasher system is on.

 Windshield Wiper/Washer Switch 

The wiper control switch is mounted on the right - hand side of the steering column. The windshield wipers and washers are both controlled by the control lever.

 Ignition Switch 

The ignition switch is mounted on the steering column. The ignition switch is activated by the ignition switch lock cylinder through a pin which is part of the ignition switch. The ignition switch lock cylinder also controls the mechanism that provides a positive lock for the steering system. The lock mechanism is located in the steering column lock housing.

SECTION 412-00: Climate Control System - General Information

1999 Contour/Mystique Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Climate Control System

The purpose of the climate control system is to route air to the designated registers. This is accomplished when air enters the plenum through the fresh/recirculated air inlet and is routed to the desired outlets by the use of distribution doors.

The air distribution system contains the heater core, A/C evaporator core, blower motor and all of the distribution doors. All of the air is mixed and distributed inside of the plenum assembly, depending on the distribution door positions.

The Plenum Assembly

[FIGURE: GL1100A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

-

Outside Air Inlet

2

-

Recirculated Air Inlet

3

-

Plenum

4

-

Floor Duct

5

-

Panel Register Outlet

For additional information, refer to Section 412-01 .

 Heating/Defrosting 

The heater system is a blended air system, receiving outside air through the air inlet, which is connected to the upper cowl. Air is directed through the heater core for heating and around for cooling, mixed and discharged through outlets in the plenum assembly to the floor, panel or defrost nozzles, as desired.

For additional information, refer to Section 412-02 .

 Heater Core 

The heater core consists of a number of fins and tubes in an arrangement to extract heat from the engine coolant and transfer that heat to the air that passes through the heater core.

 Blower Motor 

The blower motor pulls air from the air inlet and forces it into the plenum assembly where it is mixed and distributed. The blower motor has four speeds and is controlled by the blower motor switch and resistor.

 Air Conditioning 

The R-134a air conditioning (A/C) system uses a hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) (non-CFC) based refrigerant and a special refrigerant oil. Do not use R-12 tools and equipment when repairing an R-134a system unless specified in the workshop manual. Never mix R-12 and R-134a refrigerants and oils. They are not compatible.

 A/C System 

The A/C system is a multi-piece, single case design, with an integral blower. The system allows the operator to control the temperature by delivering heated or cooled air to maintain a constant vehicle comfort level. In addition, during A/C operation, it reduces the relative humidity of the air inside the vehicle. Controls are provided to adjust the temperature and system functions, including blower motor speeds for desired airflow. Outside air is drawn from the cowl air inlet just below the windshield during all system operations except for MAX A/C cooling (when recirculated air is used) and OFF. Temperature control can be maintained in all control settings except when the system is turned OFF. For additional information, refer to Section 412-03 .

 Control System Inputs 

The climate control system inputs are selected manually from the climate control assembly.

 Control System Outputs 

The air management doors are controlled by vacuum control actuators and an electronic blend door motor. The air inlet and distribution doors are controlled by vacuum control actuators. The temperature blend door is controlled by the electronic motor.

The electronic blend door motor provides a infinite number of temperature blend door positions. Temperature control position energizes the electronic motor moving the temperature blend door.

Vacuum control actuators are used on both air distribution and air inlet doors. Vacuum control actuators are controlled by the climate control assembly through the engine vacuum.

For additional information, refer to Section 412-04 .

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Flourescent Dye Leak Detection

 Special Tool(s) 

[FIGURE: ST1261A.gif]

120 Watt UV Spot Lamp or equivalent

164-R0721

[FIGURE: ST1460A.gif]

R-134a Manifold Gauge Set or equivalent

023-R0046 (176-R032A)

 NOTE: Since 07/99 vehicles have a fluorescent tracer dye tablet inserted into the A/C system. If tracer dye is present, there is a green cross on the suction accumulator.

 NOTE: If it is necessary to add tracer dye, use the dye injector. A/C systems require 7.4 ml (0.25 oz) of Fluoro-Light/P Fluorescent Tracer Dye.

 NOTE: Some vehicles may have signs of refrigerant oil at the spring lock couplers. This may be caused from the assembly process which applies to the fittings before installation to aid in assembly. When a spring lock coupler is suspected of leaking, always wipe the fitting clean and verify the leak with R-134a Automatic Calibration Halogen Leak Detector.

 NOTE: The exact location of leaks can be pinpointed by the bright yellow-green glow of the tracer dye. Since more than one leak may exist, always inspect each component.

Check for leaks using a 120 Watt UV Spot Lamp. Always scan all components, fittings and lines of the A/C system.

After the leak is found and repaired, remove any traces of dye with a general purpose oil solvent.

Verify the repair by operating the system for some minutes and inspecting with the UV lamp again.

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Electronic Leak Detection

 Special Tool(s) 

[FIGURE: ST1245A.gif]

Automatic Calibration Halogen Leak Detector or equivalent

023-R1000

[FIGURE: ST1460A.gif]

R-134a Manifold Gauge Set or equivalent

023-R0046 (176-R032A)

 WARNING: Good ventilation before leak detection is necessary in the area where it is to be performed. If the surrounding air is contaminated with refrigerant gas, the leak detector will indicate this gas all the time. Odors from other chemicals such as antifreeze, diesel fuel, disc brake cleaner, or other cleaning solvents can cause the same problem. While leak detection air movement must be prevented. 

Attach R-134a Manifold Gauge Set to the service gauge port valves.

Leave both R-134a Manifold Gauge Set valves closed.

Both gauges should indicate 4,1-5,5 bar (413-551 kPa, 60-80 psi) at 24°C (75°F) with the engine off.

If little or no pressure is indicated, charge the system with approx. 300g of refrigerant. For additional information, refer to Drain, Evacuate and Refill the A/C System.

Use R-134a Automatic Calibration Halogen Leak Detector to leak test the refrigerant system. Follow the instructions included with leak detector for handling and operation techniques.

 NOTE: Refilling the system is only permited when the amount of refrigerant is wellknown.
If a leak is found, reclaim the refrigerant if necessary. For additional information, refer to A/C System Evacuation and Charging.

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Air Conditioning (A/C) System Recovery, Evacuation and Charging

 General Equipment 

Servicing unit

 CAUTION: The refrigerant identification equipment must be used before the system is emptied, otherwise the servicing unit may become contaminated. Contaminated refrigerant must be disposed of as special waste. The manufacturer's instructions must be followed when working with the servicing unit. 
Unscrew and remove the protective caps from the A/C charging connections.

Pull back the catch of the quick-fit union on the line of the servicing unit.

[FIGURE: E0031288.gif]

 NOTE: Larger inner diameter for high-pressure side. Smaller inner diameter for low-pressure side.
Connect the servicing unit line to the A/C charging connection.

 WARNING: When recovering the refrigerant do not allow it to enter the atmosphere under any circumstances. Failure to observe this instruction can lead to injuries. 

 NOTE: When removing components of the air conditioning system, calculate the residual quantity of refrigerant oil. For additional information, refer to Refilling refrigerant oil.
Empty the air conditioning system through the low-pressure connection according to the instructions of the servicing unit manufacturer.

 CAUTION: The air conditioning system must be evacuated for about 30 minutes before recharging it, to ensure that it operates correctly. 

 CAUTION: If moisture was able to enter an open system over an extended period (several hours), install a new accumulator/dehydrator and increase the evacuation time to 2-3 hours. 
Evacuate the air conditioning system according to the instructions of the servicing unit manufacturer.

 NOTE: If an air conditioning system that was filled with refrigerant is being evacuated, then some refrigerant will still be in the refrigerant oil in the compressor. This residual amount of refrigerant may still evaporate and during the leak test may result in a slight increase in the pressure gauge reading (max. two sub-divisions). However, despite this pressure increase the air conditioning system is free from leaks.

 NOTE: If the gauge reading increases by more than 20 mbar (2 kPa or 0.29 psi), the system is leaking.
Perform the leak test.

For the leak test, close the manual valves on the gauge set, switch off the servicing unit vacuum pump and watch the low pressure gauge.

If there are leaks, charge the air conditioning system with approx. 300 g of refrigerant and check it using leak testing equipment. For additional information, refer to Leak testing.

Refill with refrigerant oil. For additional information, refer to Refilling with refrigerant oil.

 CAUTION: The air conditioning system must always be evacuated before charging. 

 NOTE: Depending on the type of servicing unit and the variant (with or without heated filling cylinder), the air conditioning system is either charged with liquid through the high-pressure connection or with gas through the low-pressure connection,

 NOTE: Charge quantity on sticker in the engine compartment.
Charging the air conditioning system (with liquid) through the high-pressure connection.

Open the shut-off valve on the high-pressure side.

Switch the servicing unit to "Fill" mode and charge with the prescribed quantity of liquid refrigerant (R134a).

[FIGURE: W3402025.gif]

 CAUTION: Only gaseous charging of the air conditioning system is done through the low-pressure connection. 
Charging the air conditioning system through the low-pressure connection.

Open the shut-off valve on the low-pressure side.

Switch the servicing unit to "Fill" mode and charge with gaseous refrigerant.

Add the remaining amount of refrigerant with the air conditioning switched on. To do so run the engine at about 1200-1500 rev/min. Set the air conditioning system to full cooling power and fresh air mode. Set the blower to full power. Charge with the remainder of the prescribed charge quantity.

 WARNING: Do not detach the high-pressure hose when the air conditioning is switched on. Failure to observe this instruction can lead to injuries. 
Disconnecting the servicing unit.
